curation.lead:
Brad S. Karp (born circa 1960) served as chairman of Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison LLP from 2008 until his resignation on February 4, 2026, following the Department of Justice release of Jeffrey Epstein's email corpus. DOJ Volume 11 documents show that Karp maintained both a personal and professional relationship with Epstein from at least 2014 through early 2019, visiting Epstein's townhouse at 9 East 71st Street repeatedly and dining with him alongside Kathryn Ruemmler, the former White House Counsel. Karp's firm simultaneously represented Leon Black and Apollo Global Management, SoftBank, and Nissan interests in the Carlos Ghosn prosecution. Emails show Karp discussed all of these representations directly with Epstein: forwarding a response about a Leon Black escrow arrangement (March 2016), responding when Epstein asked about the Caesars litigation while Paul Weiss was a named defendant in Case 15-01145, and confirming SoftBank representation when Epstein asked "Rajeev misra do you represent?" in January 2019 (EFTA02627034). Epstein characterized the bond in a November 2018 email: "You and i are friends with a disagreement" (EFTA02617307).

The correspondence around the Ghosn affair provides the most detailed documentary thread. Karp told Epstein he was "dealing with Ghosn crisis" the day after the arrest (EFTA02616157), and within ten days the two were exchanging intelligence on the matter in both directions. Paul Weiss registered as a lobbyist for Ghosn under the Lobbying Disclosure Act, with Karp personally named on the filing. Quarterly LDA filings show $240,000 in declared income from Q4 2018 through Q1 2020.

The relationship extended into Karp's family life. Both children appear in the email corpus: his son David attended Epstein-hosted Woody Allen screenings beginning at age eighteen in May 2014 and later dined privately with Epstein and Allen (EFTA02347847). Karp shared his daughter Meredith's medical emergency with Epstein (EFTA02477831) and brought his son's girlfriend to Epstein events. His wife Robbie Karp is referenced obliquely but never named in the documents. The breadth of personal disclosures in these emails — children's careers, family medical information, a wife's private opinions — goes well beyond the scope of a conventional attorney-client relationship.

Email records indicate the two exchanged information across multiple active representations, combining personal friendship, legal advisory work, and informal information sharing in ways that blurred conventional professional boundaries.

sections.title: The Ghosn Intelligence Channel
sections.content:
The Karp-Epstein correspondence on the Carlos Ghosn arrest provides the most granular documentary evidence of two-way information sharing in the DOJ email corpus. Karp told Epstein he was "dealing with Ghosn crisis" on November 20, 2018, the day after the arrest (EFTA02616157). Within ten days, Epstein offered information from his own source: "ghosen info when you like." Karp replied: "That was quick. On call with DOJ now" — indicating both that Karp was in contact with the Department of Justice on Ghosn-related matters and that he noted the speed with which Epstein had obtained information (EFTA02612503). Epstein's response, comparing his source to "the experienced mechanic" who knows "exactly where to knock," suggests a specific source rather than general media monitoring.

The December 26, 2018 exchange is particularly detailed. Epstein wrote: "following ghosen. it appears my guy had it right from day one. any updates?" Karp, returning from Tokyo, replied: "Just returning from tokyo. Your guy totally had it right" (EFTA02609103). Karp's Christmas-period trip to Tokyo in his capacity as Paul Weiss chairman reflects the seniority of the firm's involvement in the Ghosn matter. Four days later, Epstein followed up: "how you doing? traveling to tokyo must have been stressful" (EFTA02608327). The casual tone of these exchanges — checking in on the stress of international travel, sharing assessments in informal fragments — indicates a relationship in which the chairman of a major law firm regularly discussed an ongoing DOJ matter with Epstein and validated the accuracy of Epstein's independent source.

The thread continued into late January 2019. On January 24, Epstein told Karp: "when free I can bring you up to date on google. ghosen SIC and..." (EFTA02626821) — offering updates on multiple matters at once, including one involving Google and the ongoing Ghosn situation. Two days later, on January 26, Epstein wrote "ghosen a very very not good guy" and asked: "Rajeev misra do you represent?" (EFTA02627034). Karp replied: "Sort of. Spoke to him yesterday." Epstein then told a third party: "brad represent softbank, not rajeev, but did speak to him yesterday, re DB" — indicating that Karp had also discussed Deutsche Bank matters with Rajeev Misra. The same day, Reid Weingarten independently asked Epstein about Misra, placing Epstein as an intermediary between Karp (representing SoftBank) and Weingarten (seeking information on Misra) — with neither necessarily aware of the other's full involvement.

sections.title: Leon Black and the Apollo Exposure
sections.content:
Karp's relationship with Leon Black through Epstein involved overlapping professional and personal obligations. In March 2016, Karp forwarded to Epstein a Paul Weiss internal exchange about Black's request to establish a $2 million escrow fund at the firm "from which payments would be made monthly pursuant to a contract with an individual" (EFTA02470157). Paul Weiss partner Bruce Birenboim declined to serve as escrow agent, but the email places Karp as the point of contact between Black's financial requests and Epstein. A November 2016 three-way billing email among Karp, Epstein, and Black addressed which party was paying for Paul Weiss, Akin Gump, Deloitte, and PwC services, indicating that the advisory fee structures were intertwined.

When Epstein discovered in August 2016 that all three Apollo co-founders — Black, Joshua Harris, and Marc Rowan — had failed to properly file IRS Form 8865 for the BRH Holdings foreign partnership, it was Karp at Paul Weiss whom Epstein contacted. Karp responded: "First I have heard of this." The 8865 compliance failure carried open statutes of limitation extending back to 2007, and Steven Pesner at Akin Gump was placed on the advisory team alongside Karp. Separately in August 2016, Epstein emailed Karp: "is Caesars getting better or worse?" (EFTA02452879). At that time, Paul Weiss was counsel to CEC and Apollo in the CEOC restructuring and was a named defendant in Case 15-01145, which alleged the firm simultaneously represented Apollo, CEC, and CEOC while engineering fraudulent asset transfers. A court-appointed examiner found Paul Weiss had a conflict of interest. Karp's discussion of even the general trajectory of the Caesars litigation with Epstein — a non-party with no privilege claim — represents a potential breach of attorney-client confidentiality that, based on the email record, predates the Ghosn-related disclosures by more than two years.

Karp also worked with Epstein on matters involving Marc Rowan. Epstein engaged Karp on Apollo/Athene restructuring matters, with Ruemmler recommending hires at Paul Weiss in connection with the work (EFTA02386047). Taken together, the Caesars exchange, the 8865 crisis, the Black escrow, and the Rowan advisory indicate that Karp functioned as Epstein's primary institutional contact within the firm, routing work and sharing information across what would typically be firewalled client relationships.

sections.title: The Personal Entanglement
sections.content:
The email record indicates that the Karp-Epstein relationship was personal as well as professional. Karp's visits to 71st Street were regular and informal: arriving two minutes late from a board meeting on July 11, 2017 (EFTA02218810), having appointments rescheduled by Lesley Groff when Epstein had "an appt outside the house" (EFTA02261421), receiving hand-delivered packages (EFTA02247503). On May 19, 2017, Epstein arranged a dinner at the townhouse with Karp and Kathryn Ruemmler, the former White House Counsel who later became Goldman Sachs General Counsel. Karp replied: "I can join for about an hour" (EFTA02213590).

The relationship extended to Karp's family. In May 2014, both Karp children — David, then approximately eighteen, and Meredith — attended an Epstein-hosted Woody Allen screening alongside Eva and Glenn Dubin and Jes Staley's family (EFTA02383641). By January 2016, David Karp had dined privately with Epstein and met Allen in person (EFTA02347847). Epstein later arranged for Allen to write out answers to David's personal questions as a gift, and facilitated introductions between David and Allen's assistant Helen Robin in August 2016. Karp brought his son's girlfriend, Courtney Loo, to Epstein screenings in January 2018. When Meredith Karp suffered a severe allergic reaction, Karp shared the details with Epstein (EFTA02477831). In November 2017, when the Charlie Rose sexual harassment allegations broke, Epstein sent Karp the Washington Post article that evening, writing: "I guess your wife can feel vindicated" and referencing his own connection to the Rose situation through someone who had warned Rose his behavior would "get both he and me in trouble" (EFTA02563643, EFTA02563707).

When the relationship encountered friction, Epstein's language reflected its personal nature. On November 2, 2018, he wrote to Karp: "This is silly. You and i are friends with a disagreement. We should not allow this to get blown out of proportion" (EFTA02617307). Karp replied: "I would send" — an apparent reference to advising on how to handle the dispute. Separately, in January 2019, Epstein instructed Karp regarding a financial negotiation with an unnamed third party: "if he brings up the money issue please stand tough and tell him you had told" (EFTA02608729). During this period Karp was simultaneously involved in the Ghosn lobbying campaign and representing SoftBank, accumulating multiple concurrent roles involving Epstein.

sections.title: The Weingarten Shadow Advisory
sections.content:
Reid Weingarten, the Steptoe & Johnson white-collar defense attorney who would later represent Epstein in his 2019 federal case, maintained a concealed advisory relationship with Karp that Epstein deliberately managed. Weingarten told Epstein in 2015: "do not mention my role with brad" (EFTA02341191). The nature of this undisclosed role is not fully explained in the available documents, but its existence transforms the map of the Karp-Epstein relationship. Epstein was not merely sharing intelligence with Karp; he was simultaneously running a back-channel advisory arrangement through Weingarten that Karp may not have known about, or that both men were keeping off the record.

The two channels converged in late January 2019. On January 26, the same day Karp confirmed his SoftBank representation to Epstein, Weingarten independently emailed Epstein asking about Misra: "Rajeev misra...softbank vision fund...any special jeffrey insights here?" (HOUSE_OVERSIGHT_028601). Epstein then told a third party: "obviously dont mention my role with brad till we both think it useful" — revealing that Epstein was actively managing the disclosure of his Karp relationship to Ron Soffer, who was being considered for Misra's side of the SoftBank dispute. Epstein functioned as a hub connecting Karp (SoftBank's lawyer), Weingarten (seeking intelligence for a potential Misra engagement), and Soffer (a potential Israeli lawyer for Misra) — while none of the three necessarily knew the full scope of the others' involvement. By Q3 2019, Weingarten was added to the Paul Weiss Ghosn lobbying registration, formalizing what had been a covert arrangement into an official engagement.

sections.title: Surveillance and Private Intelligence
sections.content:
Karp served as Epstein's primary interface to the private investigation industry. On March 30, 2019 — less than four months before Epstein's final arrest — Epstein asked Karp: "is your go to investigators kroll?" Karp replied: "I use Nardello, who I think is better at these types of matters" (EFTA02637332). The phrasing "these types of matters" is ambiguous but significant: it implies Karp had discussed with Epstein the specific nature of the investigation for which Epstein was seeking resources, and had rendered a professional judgment about which firm was best suited. Nardello & Co., founded by former federal prosecutor Daniel Nardello, is a corporate intelligence firm specializing in due diligence, asset tracing, and litigation support.

Karp's deployment of Nardello extended beyond this March 2019 recommendation. The investigation database records that Karp coordinated Nardello surveillance in connection with Leon Black's dispute with Guzel Ganieva in 2015 (EFTA02384875). This establishes a multi-year pattern in which Karp functioned as Epstein's and Black's shared procurement channel for private intelligence services. The relationship also had an intelligence-receiving dimension: Karp was the contact through whom Epstein discussed "subjects: leon, kathy boies" in October 2018, suggesting Epstein was brokering intelligence about Leon Black, Kathy Ruemmler, and David Boies to or through Karp. The aggregation of these roles — procuring investigators, receiving intelligence briefs, sharing privileged client information, and validating Epstein's independent intelligence sources — places Karp at the operational center of Epstein's legal-intelligence apparatus, not at its periphery.
